title: React Router DOM
summary: Adds pages to a single-page app with react-router-dom: createBrowserRouter and RouterProvider set up routes, App becomes a layout that renders child pages through <Outlet />, Link moves between pages without a reload, and a Not Found / error page catches bad URLs. Step-by-step guide arrives when the lecture is published.
goal: Set up routes in a React + Vite app with a layout, navigation links and an error page.

steps.title: Read both lessons
steps.detail: Read 'Intro to React-Router-Dom' and 'Adding Navigation and Pages', especially 'Understanding the Mental Model'.
steps.doneWhen: You can explain what <Outlet /> does in App.jsx.

steps.title: Build the curriculum's router in a scratch app
steps.detail: In a throwaway Vite app, npm install react-router-dom, create src/pages/HomePage.jsx, then add this src/router.jsx and render <RouterProvider router={router} /> in main.jsx.
steps.doneWhen: Visiting / shows App's layout with HomePage inside it.

steps.title: Add an About page and a 404
steps.detail: Add an about route, a <Link to="/about"> in App, and an errorElement on the root route. Then visit a made-up URL.
steps.doneWhen: Clicking the link switches pages without a full reload, and a bad URL shows your error page.

steps.title: Imagine routes for Myflix
steps.detail: Myflix has one view (assignments/week-02/netflix/src/views/MyList.jsx) and no router. List the pages you'd want (for example /, /lists/:id, /title/:id). This sets up the next lecture on route parameters.
steps.doneWhen: You have a list of 3 or more Myflix routes.

concepts.meaning: Changing pages in the browser without asking the server for a new HTML page.
The config that maps each URL path to a component.
The spot in a layout where the current child page appears.
The default child page shown at the parent's exact path.
The component shown when a route fails or the URL doesn't match.
